objectives: Describe the roles, data model and risky commands of DNP3 and EtherNet/IP with CIP
Name the common weaknesses that most industrial protocols share with Modbus
Identify the industrial protocols the CybICS PLC exposes and confirm them with nmap and Wireshark
takeaways: DNP3 (TCP 20000) connects a master to outstations in utilities; EtherNet/IP (TCP 44818, UDP 2222) carries CIP objects in factories.
Most industrial protocols were designed for closed networks and have no authentication or encryption by default.
Security extensions such as DNP3 Secure Authentication and CIP Security exist, but older devices often cannot use them.
The CybICS PLC exposes Modbus, S7comm, DNP3 and EtherNet/IP over the same memory, so blocking one port does not protect the data.
An nmap service name with a question mark is a guess from the port number; a Wireshark dissector confirms the protocol.

checkpoints.question: An EtherNet/IP client must send Register Session before anything else. Does this protect the device?
options: Yes, Register Session works like a password login
No, any client is handed a session handle
Yes, the session handle encrypts what follows
checkpoints.explanation: Register Session just hands out a handle so replies can be matched to a client. A mandatory first step looks like a login, but there is no password and no encryption. That would need CIP Security, which many devices do not support.

checkpoints.question: nmap reports 44818/tcp open EtherNetIP-2? on the CybICS PLC. What does the question mark tell you?
options: The port is probably filtered or closed
nmap guessed the service from the port number
The service answered, but its traffic is encrypted
checkpoints.explanation: The question mark means nmap's probes did not get a reply it could match, so it fell back to the usual service for that port. The port itself is open, as the word 'open' says. Capturing a connection and seeing Wireshark's enip dissector decode it confirms the protocol.

quiz.question: In DNP3, what is an outstation?
options: The control centre that polls the field
A field device that answers the master
A backup master that takes over on failure
A gateway that converts DNP3 to Modbus
quiz.explanation: The master is the control centre; outstations are the field devices it polls, such as a substation controller. 'Out' makes the control centre sound tempting, but it is the master. Outstations can also send unsolicited responses when a value changes, which is useful over slow links.

quiz.question: A firewall blocks port 502 on the CybICS PLC. Can an attacker on the network still reach the PLC's memory?
options: No, the PLC's memory is only reachable over Modbus
Yes, over S7comm, DNP3 or EtherNet/IP on the PLC
Only through the OPC-UA server, which mirrors values
Only with physical access to the PLC cabinet
quiz.explanation: OpenPLC enables four industrial servers that map onto the same memory, so closing one port leaves the others open. The OPC-UA server is a separate container that itself reads the PLC over Modbus. A rule that blocks the attacker's address as a whole closes all of the PLC's ports.

quiz.question: Which weaknesses do DNP3, EtherNet/IP and BACnet commonly share with Modbus? (Select all that apply)
options: No authentication by default
Traffic is not encrypted by default
Built-in discovery that reveals device details
No secure extension exists for any of them in the standard
quiz.explanation: All three were designed for trusted networks: no authentication or encryption by default, and broadcast discovery such as List Identity or Who-Is. Secure extensions do exist (DNP3 Secure Authentication, CIP Security, BACnet Secure Connect); the problem is that they are rarely switched on.

quiz.question: You need to find PROFINET devices on a factory network. Why will an nmap port scan from another subnet not help?
options: PROFINET hides behind an unusually high TCP port
Its real-time frames carry no IP header at all
PROFINET devices silently drop every scan packet
PROFINET only uses UDP, which nmap cannot scan
quiz.explanation: PROFINET real-time and DCP discovery frames use EtherType 0x8892 directly on Ethernet. With no IP header they never cross a router, and a port scanner has no ports to probe. A high port or UDP would still be scannable; you have to listen on the same segment.

quiz.question: nmap shows port 102 open on an unknown device. What can you conclude?
options: It is a Siemens S7 PLC, since 102 is the S7 port
It may be S7comm or IEC 61850 MMS; look closer
It is a DNP3 outstation on its default port
It is an IEC 60870-5-104 station in a substation
quiz.explanation: Both S7comm and IEC 61850 MMS run over ISO transport on TCP port 102, so a port number is a hint, not proof. DNP3 normally uses 20000 and IEC 104 uses 2404. An nmap script such as s7-info or a Wireshark capture tells you which one it is.

quiz.question: Which two bytes start every DNP3 link-layer frame, so you can spot DNP3 in a hex dump?
options: AB CD
quiz.explanation: DNP3 frames begin with 05 64. The bytes 03 00 start a TPKT header, which is what S7comm uses, and 00 00 is the protocol identifier inside a Modbus TCP header, so they are easy to confuse.
